gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Loud, stretched-out letters with tapering ink ends. Noto Sans Saurashtra stays plain sans underneath, and if Warnes were shrunk down, its spacious tracking would lose the drama the body text never needs.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-sc: Expressive from the first glyph, Warnes lays down every stroke at a single width, like a fixed brush. And Noto Sans SC follows with modern, chalk-soft curves that stop short of closing, so the two never fight for attention.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Warnes stretches out wide and bold, every stroke the same thickness, ink tapering off before the ends meet. Noto Sans Sharada takes over with bulky lowercase and open c forms, so a long passage feels sturdy and easy going.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Noto Sans Siddham reads contemporary and approachable, with a large central band and an s whose ends hang far from its spine. Warnes does the loud, wire-thin display work; Siddham does the quiet reading.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Warnes is all bold, stretched letters with no thick or thin strokes, built to make noise. Noto Sans Sinhala does the opposite job, laying a dark, steady stripe of lowercase with curve endings that keep their distance.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo reads modern and businesslike, with a sizable x-height and curved letters whose mouths stay wide open. Its strongest trait is how Warnes shouts, wire-bold, above it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Noto Sans Sundanese reads clean and quiet, with open-mouthed e crossbars and capitals barely taller than the lowercase. Warnes sits above in bold, stretched strokes of one thickness, so the heading performs while the plain sans just carries the words.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Rope-thick curves, spread wide and bold. But Noto Sans Sunuwar, a plain sans with open curves and short ascender stems, keeps the page friendly once the heading has made its entrance.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Warnes draws every letter as one monoline stroke, bold and stretched, with ink tapering off before touching. And Noto Syloti Nagri's short ascenders and tall x-height give it a sturdy partner.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Warnes draws every stroke like a technical pen, steady and bold. Noto Sans Syriac then follows with rounded, glassy lowercase bowls and easy s turns, which soften the heading's stretched-out swagger.
